beats.say: An agent that acts inside your web app needs authority. Today that means an API key: every record, every field, until someone remembers to revoke it.
Nobody means forever, everything. They mean: these two accounts, these two fields, the next ten minutes. Nothing today turns that sentence into that grant.

beats.caption: Relay CRM — the host application
beats.say: This is Relay CRM. Ordinary business software. Mandate is not part of it. It's a capability layer installed into it, and right now it is doing nothing.

beats.caption: Selection proposes. It grants nothing.
beats.say: Selecting proposes a scope. It grants nothing. Two accounts picked, and the inspector still shows only the two read-only tools. Nothing appeared.

beats.caption: The human delegates: 2 accounts, 2 fields, 10 minutes
beats.say: Now the human delegates. These accounts, these two fields, ten minutes.

beats.caption: document.modelContext.registerTool(...)
beats.say: Three things change at once. The rows take the authority ring, the panel states the exact scope, and the browser registers a tool that did not exist a second ago — its schema a readout of what the human just decided.

beats.caption: executeTool(mandate_stage_account_update, { c-northwind, status })
beats.say: The agent calls it through the browser's own WebMCP API. The change is staged, marked as the agent's. Nothing is committed.

beats.caption: executeTool(... { c-kestrel }) → OUT_OF_SCOPE
beats.say: Now ask that tool for an account that was selected but never delegated. Refused. Out of scope, decided by the server.

beats.caption: executeTool(... { c-atlas, field: arr }) → OUT_OF_SCOPE
beats.say: These notes contain a pasted email telling the assistant to approve everything. Run the call it asks for. Refused. Authority does not come from text.

beats.caption: Narrowed mid-flight → mandate v2
beats.say: Narrow the mandate mid-flight. Version two publishes; the agent still believes in version one. Refused — policy changed. The schema was a courtesy. This is enforcement.

beats.caption: Revoked → NO_ACTIVE_MANDATE
beats.say: Revoke it. The same call gets a different refusal: no active mandate. Two refusals, two reasons, both from the server.

beats.caption: There is no apply tool, and no route behind one
beats.say: And the most consequential act has no agent path at all. No apply tool, and no route behind one.

beats.caption: Only a human applies
beats.say: The human validates, and applies. The values land in the CRM.

beats.caption: The product: no panel, just the pill
beats.say: Everything you have seen is instrumentation for this explanation. The product underneath has no panel: a pill that cannot be hidden, and a popover where the decision is.

beats.caption: Same layer, different host → mandate_stage_service_update
beats.say: And none of this knows what a CRM is. Same session, a different host: a deployment console. The records change, the fields change, and the tool renames itself. Not one line of the server changed.

beats.caption: ChatGPT desktop — site tools — real executeTool calls
beats.say: Not simulated. That is ChatGPT's own browser, calling the tools this page registered. It stages what the mandate allows. The server refuses a record outside the scope, then a field no mandate can cover. Asked to commit, it answers that there is no apply tool. A human presses the button.

beats.caption: Human intent, compiled into a live WebMCP contract
beats.say: Mandate turns explicit, temporary human intent into a live WebMCP contract that the server enforces on every call.
